problems.title: Sum of two cosines
problems.question: Simplify cos(α+β)+cos(α−β).
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: Adding the plus and minus versions cancels the sine products, leaving 2cosαcosβ.

problems.title: Product to a sine sum
problems.question: Express 2sinαcosβ as a sum.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Add the sine angle-addition and angle-subtraction formulas.
steps: sin(α+β)+sin(α−β)=2sinαcosβ, since the cosαsinβ terms cancel.

problems.title: Difference of cosines
problems.question: Factor cosα−cosβ.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: Subtracting the two cosine formulas gives −2sin u sin v.

problems.title: A sine quotient gives tangent addition
problems.question: Simplify sin(α+β)/(cosαcosβ).
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: Divide both terms by cosαcosβ to get tanα+tanβ. The original domain requires cosαcosβ≠0.

problems.title: A rhombus base equal to a diagonal-section area
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has a rhombus base of side 1,acute angle 60°. The base and smaller diagonal section have equal area. Find lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: The diagonal section is a rectangle of width 1 and prism height h, so equality gives h=√3/2.
Lateral area=base perimeter×h=4×√3/2=2√3.

problems.title: Amplitude of a sine-cosine sum
problems.question: Find the maximum of 3sinx+4cosx.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: The bound is √25=5. Equality is reached when sinx=3/5 and cosx=4/5, a valid unit-circle point.

problems.title: Factor three sine terms
problems.question: Factor sinx−siny+sin(x−y).
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: sinx−siny=2cos((x+y)/2)sin((x−y)/2). Also sin(x−y)=2sin((x−y)/2)cos((x−y)/2).
Factor their common sine, then use cos((x+y)/2)+cos((x−y)/2)=2cos(x/2)cos(y/2).

problems.title: A triangle across a right prism
problems.question: A right triangular prism has right base ABC with AC=1,BC=1.5 and height √3/2. Find area ACB₁.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: CB₁=√(9/4+3/4)=√3. AC is perpendicular both to BC and the prism’s vertical direction, so it is perpendicular to CB₁.
The triangle area is AC·CB₁/2=√3/2.

problems.title: Sum the space diagonals of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Every edge of a regular hexagonal prism is b. Find the sum of all space-diagonal lengths.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Each bottom vertex joins three nonadjacent top vertices not lying with it on a face.
steps: Two diagonals from each bottom vertex project to base chords √3b, so their lengths are √(3b²+b²)=2b. The third projects to 2b, giving length √5b.
Across six bottom vertices, the sum is 6(2×2b+√5b)=24b+6√5b. Each space diagonal is counted once.

problems.title: Euler’s polyhedron relation
problems.question: A polyhedral body has 20 vertices and 36 edges. Find its face count under the usual single closed, sphere-like polyhedron assumption.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: F=2−20+36=18. This is the standard textbook polyhedron model.

problems.title: Parallel projection preserves a trapezoid
problems.question: Which listed polygon can be a nondegenerate parallel projection of a trapezoid?
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: A nondegenerate planar affine projection preserves parallelism and nonparallelism of line pairs.
steps: The parallel bases stay parallel, and the nonparallel legs stay nonparallel. Therefore the image remains a trapezoid. A degenerate projection can collapse to a segment, which is not one of the listed polygons.

problems.title: A cosine graph’s vertical intercept
problems.question: Find the y-axis intercept ordinate of y=2cos(2x−π/4)+1.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.

problems.title: A right prism from a smaller diagonal inclination
problems.question: A right prism has parallelogram base sides 1,2,height 3. Its smaller space diagonal makes 60° with the base. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: 3=5−4|cosθ| gives |cosθ|=1/2 and sinθ=√3/2. Base area=1×2×√3/2=√3.
Lateral area=2(1+2)×3=18. Total=18+2√3.

problems.title: Range after absolute value and translation
problems.question: Find the range of |2sin(3x−7)−1|+1.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Sine spans [−1,1], so the expression inside the absolute value spans [−3,1].
steps: Its absolute value spans [0,3]. Adding 1 gives [1,4], with both endpoints attained.

problems.title: Sufficient parity conditions versus necessary ones
problems.question: For [f(sin2x)−g(cos3x)]h(tan1.5x), which listed parity assumptions guarantee evenness?
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Composing any function with an even inner function is even; composing an even function with an odd inner function is even on the symmetric domain.
steps: sin2x and tan1.5x are odd, while cos3x is even. If f and h are even, both f(sin2x) and h(tan1.5x) are even; g(cos3x) is even for any g.
Their difference and product are therefore even. This is a sufficient condition. It is not necessary: h≡0 makes the expression even regardless of f or g.
problems.note: If the printed wording is read as asking what follows necessarily from the final function being even, none of these parity restrictions is forced. The listed intended option supplies sufficient conditions instead.

problems.title: An exact product of three sines
problems.question: Calculate sin20°sin40°sin80°.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: At t=20°, sin60°=4sin20°sin80°sin40°. Divide √3/2 by 4 to get √3/8.

problems.title: An exact product of four cosines
problems.question: Calculate cos20°cos40°cos60°cos80°.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: At t=20°, sin160°=sin20°, so cos20°cos40°cos80°=1/8.
Multiplying by cos60°=1/2 gives 1/16.

problems.title: Commensurate frequencies give a period
problems.question: Which listed k makes sin(√2x)+sin(kx) periodic?
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Frequencies with a rational ratio have a common period.
steps: For k=1/√2, the frequency ratio is 2. A common period is 2π√2. The listed k=1,2,√3 have irrational ratios to √2 and do not work.
More generally k/√2 can be any rational number, including zero. The broad choices “all real k” and “all nonzero real k” are false.

problems.title: A square diagonal section fixes prism height
problems.question: A regular square prism has a square diagonal section. Find cosine of the angle between a space diagonal and a lateral face.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: If base side is s, the section width is s√2, so height is s√2.
steps: A space-diagonal direction is (s,s,s√2), of length 2s. Its normal component to a lateral face has length s.
Thus sinθ=1/2 and cosθ=√3/2.

problems.title: Midpoint-base prism lateral area
problems.question: A right quadrilateral prism has height 4 and base-diagonal sum 10. A second prism joins corresponding side midpoints of its bases. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Varignon midpoint-quadrilateral perimeter equals the sum of the original diagonal lengths.
steps: The new base perimeter is 10. Its height remains 4 and it is right, so lateral area=10×4=40.

problems.title: Prescribed range of an absolute cosine
problems.question: For which a does |a cosx+3| have range [0,a+3]?
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: The true maximum is |a|+3; its minimum is zero iff |a|≥3.
steps: Matching the upper endpoint requires |a|=a, or a≥0. Combining with |a|≥3 gives a≥3.
Conversely each a≥3 attains both zero and a+3 and all values between.

problems.title: A quadratic in a square root of cosine
problems.question: Find the range of 2cosx−3√(cosx)−3/8.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: The vertex t=3/4 gives minimum −3/2. Endpoints give −3/8 and −11/8, so the maximum is −3/8.
The range is [−3/2,−3/8].

problems.title: Count tangent poles in a finite interval
problems.question: How many discontinuities has y=3tan(2x+3) for x∈[0,2π]?
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
steps: As x spans the interval, the argument spans [3,4π+3]. The poles within are 3π/2,5π/2,7π/2,9π/2, giving four discontinuities.

problems.title: Two congruent rhombi allow two prism orientations
problems.question: An oblique triangular prism has equilateral base and two congruent rhombus lateral faces of side a. Lateral edges make 60° with the base. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Each lateral edge has length a and horizontal projection a/2. A face area is $\sqrt{a^4-(v\cdot e)^2}$, where e is its base edge.
steps: If the horizontal projection bisects the common 60° base angle internally, its angle to both edges is 30°. Each equal face has area a²√13/4; the third has area a². Total=(2+√13)a²/2, the listed intended answer.
An external-bisector projection is also possible. Its absolute cosine to each of those edges is 1/2, giving equal-face areas a²√15/4; the third face is a²√3/2. Total=(√15+√3)a²/2.
problems.note: Congruent rhombi can have supplementary included angles. The data do not specify an internal-bisector projection, so another feasible lateral area exists.

problems.title: Projection of a tilted rectangle
problems.question: A plane through a rectangle’s centre has two same-side vertices at distances 1,2. Its diagonals are 6 with smaller angle 60°. Find orthogonal projection area.
problems.idea: Use exact trigonometric identities or a coordinate projection, and verify the assumptions.
formulas: Rectangle sides are 3,3√3 and area 9√3; projected area = original area × cosine of plane angle.
steps: The two vertices must be adjacent, since opposite vertices have opposite signed heights. Edge height differences are therefore 1 and 3.

For a unit normal to the target plane, its components along rectangle sides have magnitudes 3/(3√3)=1/√3 and 1/3. Swapping these assignments would give a component 1 plus another nonzero component, impossible for a unit vector.
The normal component perpendicular to the rectangle is √(1−1/3−1/9)=√5/3. Thus projection area=9√3·√5/3=3√15.
